To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a model that learns where to attend can be trained to track objects in cluttered scenes using a deep architecture, (2) the model is capable of learning a gaze selection strategy that is robust to partial information, and (3) the model can learn to select from a continuous set of fixation points, which is a more general setting than the previous work.

(1) the identity pathway can be modeled with deep restricted Boltzmann machine architectures that learn the object identity from foveated images; (2) the control pathway can be modeled using a particle filter that learns to minimize tracking uncertainty by selecting the most informative gazes; and (3) the reward surface can be modeled with a gaussian process to expand the action set from a discrete to a continuous domain.

1) the proposed model outperforms the state-of-the-art on the challenging GazeCom dataset, and 2) a continuous-action-space gaze selection strategy based on gaussian processes is effective in the presence of partially observable information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of simultaneous tracking and recognition of an object of interest in a scene.
the development of a deep model that can learn to track and recognize an object in the presence of a large set of distractors.
the development of an attentional model that can learn to attend to objects in the world, and to learn to select fixations so as to minimize uncertainty.

the paper presents an interesting approach to object tracking and recognition.
the model presented here is an improvement over the previous one, and that it is a good starting point for future research in this area.

we have shown how to extend our previous work in a principled way to the partial information case and how to expand the action domain to a continuous setting, both with good performance and with a clear theoretical justification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed model can learn from gaze data to perform object tracking, and can do so in the presence of occlusions and partial gaze information.
we have developed an attentional model that learns where to look to track objects.

we have proposed a novel attentional model for image tracking that is driven by eye movements and that is capable of learning to select gazes that minimize tracking uncertainty in the presence of partially observable data and continuous action spaces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a model of attention can be used to improve tracking performance, even in the presence of noisy gaze data.
deep learning architectures, when used as building blocks in a more complex model, can provide a powerful framework for solving complex tasks.
deep architectures are useful in modeling the interaction between perception and control, and that they are particularly well suited to the problem of tracking objects with foveated vision.
